purpose: This is the Phase-1 'process budget' subsystem of the Hookemon (HKMN) Uniswap v4 hook: the on-chain plumbing that lets an authorized 'operations' address move the accrued 2.50% process share of swap fees out of the hook into a single-cycle custody vault (PegCycleVault), send it out to an off-chain/cross-chain route executor (Collector Crypt pack purchase -> pack open -> card sale), and bring the resulting USDG back for a role-gated pro-rata payout, with strict balance-delta and nonce/digest checks at every step and a terminal FAILED state for stuck/aborted cycles. MoneyRoles.sol is the shared two-step (propose/accept) role-authority base (treasury, operations, immutable programmable beneficiary) used by ProcessBudget and (per FeeAccounting) the hook itself. IPegCycleVault.sol and IPegCycleRouteExecutor.sol are the frozen ABI contracts between the hook, the vault, and the (still INTEGRATION_PENDING) provider-specific route executor.

files.role: Abstract contract mixed into the hook. Immutably binds one PegCycleVault at construction (validated against the constructor's programmable/treasury/operations addresses to prevent role collisions), exposes openPegCycle(cycleId) as the single entry point that debits the process fee liability, transfers the exact USDG amount to the vault, and tells the vault to confirm funding. Also layers extra role-successor restrictions on top of MoneyRoles so treasury/operations can never be rotated into the vault's authorizer/routeExecutor/usdg addresses.

Standalone immutable vault contract holding USDG for exactly one bound hook. Implements the full cycle state machine: EMPTY -> FUNDED -> OUTBOUND -> RETURNED -> PAYOUT_COMMITTED (loops back to allow re-funding) or OUTBOUND -> FAILED (dead end). Every authorization (funding, payout) is a fully-specified struct checked field-by-field against chain id, hook/vault/usdg identity, a fixed REQUIREMENTS_REVISION (56), nonce/cycleId/payoutId/returnReceiptDigest replay protection, expiry, and exact-balance-delta transfers via a hand-rolled _transferExact that requires a strict `bool` ABI return from the USDG token.

Interface/schema definition for FundingAuthorization (19 fields) and PayoutAuthorization (15 fields), the two off-chain-signed-then-on-chain-submitted authorization structs, plus the external function surface the vault exposes to the hook and to view callers.

One-function interface (executeOutbound) that the vault calls on the (not-yet-implemented) provider-specific route executor. This is the seam where Collector Crypt pack-buy / pack-open / card-sale logic must eventually plug in; today it is INTEGRATION_PENDING per the PegCycleVault docstring.

Shared abstract base: immutable 'programmable' beneficiary plus two-step (propose/accept) treasury and operations role transfer, per-cycle operations binding (_cycleOperations map, set-once), and the authorization helper functions (_authorizeProgrammableClaim, _authorizeTreasuryClaim, _authorizePayoutFunding, _authorizeHolderPayment) used by the fee-claim and payout paths elsewhere in the hook (not in this file set).

publicInterface: ProcessBudget.openPegCycle(bytes32 cycleId) external moneyPath returns (ReleasedCycle) -- only callable by current `operations` (via _bindCycleOperationsTrigger); consumes the vault's pending FundingAuthorization for cycleId, debits FeeAccounting's process liability, transfers exact USDG to the vault, confirms funding. Emits ProcessBudgetReleased(cycleId, operations, amount).
ProcessBudget.readReleasedCycle(bytes32) external view returns (ReleasedCycle) -- cycleId, amount, operationsTrigger for a released cycle.

PegCycleVault.bindHook(address hook_) external -- one-time, callable only by deploymentAuthority; verifies hook_.pegCycleVault() == address(this) before binding. Reverts HookAlreadyBound on a second call.

PegCycleVault.authorizeFunding(FundingAuthorization) external -- authorizer-only; ~20 field-level equality/nonzero/expiry/nonce/cycle checks; requires lifecycle in {EMPTY, PAYOUT_COMMITTED} and no authorization already pending. Emits FundingAuthorized.

PegCycleVault.consumeFundingAuthorization(bytes32 cycleId, address operationsTrigger) external returns (FundingAuthorization, uint256 balanceBefore) -- hook-only; snapshots pre-transfer balance, sets fundingInProgress=true, deletes pendingAuthorization.

PegCycleVault.confirmFunding(bytes32 cycleId, uint256 balanceBefore) external -- hook-only; requires balanceAfter - balanceBefore == authorization.amount exactly; moves lifecycle EMPTY/PAYOUT_COMMITTED -> FUNDED. Emits PegLegacyVaultFunded.

PegCycleVault.executeOutbound(bytes32 cycleId, bytes routeData) external -- callable only by the cycle's bound operationsTrigger; reentrancy-guarded (outboundEntered); checks keccak256(routeData) == authorization.outboundActionDigest; pushes exact `amount` USDG to routeExecutor, calls routeExecutor.executeOutbound(...), then requires the vault's own balance dropped by exactly `amount` and that USDG allowance to routeExecutor is back to 0. Moves FUNDED -> OUTBOUND. Emits PegCycleOutboundExecuted.

PegCycleVault.authorizePayout(PayoutAuthorization) external -- authorizer-only; requires lifecycle == OUTBOUND; ~18 checks including rootSum >= activeAuthorization.minimumReturnUsdg AND current USDG balance == rootSum exactly; moves OUTBOUND -> RETURNED. Emits PayoutAuthorized.

PegCycleVault.consumePayoutAuthorization(PayoutAuthorization) external returns (address operationsTrigger) -- hook-only, reentrancy-guarded (payoutEntered); re-derives keccak256(authorization) and compares to stored payoutAuthorizationDigest; pushes the entire balance (== rootSum) to the hook; requires post-balance == 0; records committed payoutId/returnReceiptDigest per cycleId; moves RETURNED -> PAYOUT_COMMITTED (which re-opens the door to a new authorizeFunding).

PegCycleVault.recordTerminalFailure(bytes32 cycleId, bytes32 failureReceiptDigest) external -- authorizer-only; requires lifecycle == OUTBOUND AND current USDG balance == 0; moves OUTBOUND -> FAILED (terminal, unrecoverable -- see suspicions). Emits TerminalFailureRecorded.

PegCycleVault view getters: readPendingAuthorization, readActiveAuthorization, isNonceConsumed, isCycleConsumed, readCommittedPayoutBinding, isPayoutIdConsumed, isReturnReceiptDigestConsumed, plus public usdg/authorizer/routeExecutor/bindingManifestDigest/deploymentAuthority/hook/lifecycle/payoutAuthorizationDigest/terminalFailureReceiptDigest.

MoneyRoles.proposeTreasury/acceptTreasury, proposeOperations/acceptOperations -- two-step handover; ProcessBudget overrides _validateRoleSuccessor to also forbid rotating treasury/operations into the vault's authorizer, and _validateOperationsSuccessor to forbid rotating operations into the vault's routeExecutor or usdg address.
MoneyRoles.readRoles(bytes32 cycleId) external view -- returns RoleState, both PendingRoleTransfer structs, and the CycleBoundOperations for cycleId.

Internal-only (not externally callable, used by code outside this file set): MoneyRoles._bindCycleOperationsTrigger/_bindCycleOperations, _authorizePayoutFunding, _authorizeHolderPayment, _authorizeProgrammableClaim/_authorizeTreasuryClaim, _currentTreasury.
invariants: Every USDG movement in both files is wrapped in an explicit before/after balanceOf check that reverts (TokenBalanceDeltaMismatch) unless the delta equals the intended amount exactly -- protects against fee-on-transfer tokens or short/rebasing behavior, at the cost of being fatally incompatible with any USDG implementation that is not a plain 1:1 ERC20.

PegCycleVault._transferExact requires the raw low-level call to return exactly 32 bytes decoding to `1` (i.e. USDG.transfer must be a standards-compliant function that returns bool true) -- reverts TokenTransferFailed otherwise. No fallback for tokens that return no data (e.g. legacy USDT-style tokens).

One nonce and one cycleId can each be consumed exactly once, globally, for the vault's lifetime (consumedNonces/consumedCycles never cleared) -- funding and payout authorizations share the same nonce space.

authorizeFunding/consumeFundingAuthorization only proceed from lifecycle EMPTY or PAYOUT_COMMITTED; every other transition requires the immediately preceding state (FUNDED->OUTBOUND->RETURNED->PAYOUT_COMMITTED, or OUTBOUND->FAILED) -- strict linear state machine, no skipping.
operations is bound to a cycleId exactly once via MoneyRoles._cycleOperations (CycleAlreadyBound guard) and can never be rebound even if operations role rotates later mid-cycle.

PegCycleVault.bindHook can only ever be called once (HookAlreadyBound) and only by the immutable deploymentAuthority; ProcessBudget's constructor cross-checks the vault's authorizer/routeExecutor/usdg against its own programmable/treasury/operations to forbid role collisions.

ProcessBudget.openPegCycle and (per FeeAccounting) all other money-moving hook functions share one single moneyPathEntered reentrancy lock (the `moneyPath` modifier), i.e. cross-function reentrancy across the whole fee/process/payout surface is blocked, not just per-function.

_debitProcessLiability requires amount <= the internally tracked processLiabilityAmount ledger (accrued via _accrueAuthenticatedSwap / _splitLiability elsewhere) and calls _requireSolvent() before and after -- the vault can never be funded for more than the hook has actually accrued and is still solvent to cover.

FeeAccounting fee split is fixed at compile time: TOTAL_FEE_BPS=300 (3.00%), PROGRAMMABLE_FEE_BPS=10 (0.10%), TREASURY_FEE_BPS=40 (0.40%); the process share is the implicit remainder (300-10-40=250, 2.50%). This matches the OWNER TARGET's repository-authoritative split (0.10% Programmable + 0.40% treasury + 2.50% process = 3.00%), confirming the repo-approved numbers are what is actually coded, NOT the owner's verbally stated '0.5% separated (0.5% treasury, 0.1% Programmable)' framing -- 0.4+0.1=0.5 only works if 'separated' is read as treasury+programmable combined, and even then the owner's own phrase 'treasury 0.5%' individually does not match the coded 0.40%.
stateTransitions: EMPTY --authorizeFunding(authorizer)--> pendingAuthorization set (lifecycle unchanged, still EMPTY/PAYOUT_COMMITTED)
FUNDED --executeOutbound(bound operationsTrigger)--> OUTBOUND (PegCycleOutboundExecuted); vault balance must have dropped by exactly `amount` and allowance to routeExecutor must be back to 0
OUTBOUND --authorizePayout(authorizer)--> RETURNED (PayoutAuthorized); requires vault's live USDG balance == authorization.rootSum exactly and rootSum >= minimumReturnUsdg
RETURNED --consumePayoutAuthorization(hook)--> PAYOUT_COMMITTED (PayoutAuthorizationConsumed); vault balance must go to exactly 0; PAYOUT_COMMITTED re-enables authorizeFunding for a new cycle

OUTBOUND --recordTerminalFailure(authorizer)--> FAILED (TerminalFailureRecorded); requires vault balance == 0; FAILED has NO outgoing transition anywhere in the contract -- once entered, authorizeFunding/consumeFundingAuthorization permanently revert InvalidLifecycle for the rest of the vault's existence
externalDependencies: packages/contracts/src/accounting/FeeAccounting.sol (abstract base, read for context, not in this unit's file list) -- supplies moneyPath modifier/reentrancy flag, _debitProcessLiability, _transferExactUsdg, the TOTAL/PROGRAMMABLE/TREASURY_FEE_BPS constants, and the virtual _currentTreasuryBeneficiary/_usdgBalanceOf/_transferUsdg hooks that ProcessBudget/the concrete hook must implement.

USDG token at bindings/robinhood-chain.json 0x5fc5360D0400a0Fd4f2af552ADD042D716F1d168 (6 decimals, UUPS upgradeable proxy) -- PegCycleVault only checks usdg_.code.length>0 at construction, never verifies decimals or actual ERC20 return-data behavior on-chain; relies on IPegCycleUsdg.transfer returning a strict abi-encoded bool.

IPegCycleRouteExecutor -- the Collector-Crypt/Relay/bridge integration is INTEGRATION_PENDING per the PegCycleVault docstring; no concrete implementation exists in this file set (the legacy codex/mainnet-cycle-canary branch has a real Collector Crypt API client / Relay bridge client / MetaMask Solana signer, but that branch is explicitly non-authoritative).
deploymentAuthority (PegCycleVault constructor param) -- an off-chain-controlled EOA/multisig that performs the one-time bindHook call; no on-chain governance/timelock visible in this file set.

Off-chain authorizer signing pipeline that produces FundingAuthorization/PayoutAuthorization structs -- not present in this file set; the contracts only verify structural/replay validity, not any cryptographic signature (authorization comes from msg.sender == authorizer, i.e. authorizer is a single trusted on-chain address that submits calldata directly, not an off-chain-signed relayed authorization).

Corresponding compiled artifacts exist at packages/contracts/out/{MoneyRoles,ProcessBudget,PegCycleVault}.t.sol/*.json, meaning these tests have compiled successfully against current sources at some point. Per task constraints, forge test was NOT run in this session (a baseline run was stated to be in progress elsewhere and concurrent runs corrupt the cache), so pass/fail status of the 44 tests against the current commit (5b365c8) could not be independently confirmed here; per the pre-established repo facts, CI on the three open PRs is red for reasons unrelated to these specific test files (Foundry version-string mismatch on PR #1, and a deterministic-state-projection/STATE.md drift check on PR #2/#3), not because of failures inside these Solidity unit tests.
autonomyGaps: FAILED is a true dead end: no function anywhere in PegCycleVault.sol transitions lifecycle out of FAILED. Because bindHook is one-time and the vault is immutable-1:1 with its hook, a single terminal failure (bridge/relay failure, card unsellable, any scenario the authorizer flags via recordTerminalFailure) permanently bricks that hook's entire process-budget path -- there is no on-chain 'restart/kick a stuck cycle' primitive for this failure mode at all. The owner's dashboard requirement to 'restart/kick cycles that got stuck' has no corresponding contract-level function to call for this specific (arguably most important) stuck case; recovery would require deploying an entirely new PegCycleVault (and, since ProcessBudget's `pegCycleVault` is immutable, an entirely new hook too).

No degraded/partial-return recovery path: authorizePayout requires the vault's live balance to equal `rootSum` exactly and `rootSum >= minimumReturnUsdg`; recordTerminalFailure requires balance == exactly 0. Any outcome where less-than-minimum-but-nonzero USDG comes back from the outbound leg (e.g. a bridge fee eats into the return, or a partial fill) satisfies neither condition, leaving the cycle stuck in OUTBOUND indefinitely with no contract-level way to sweep, write off, or force-fail it.

No batching/scheduling/interval logic anywhere in this file set: openPegCycle, executeOutbound, authorizePayout, consumePayoutAuthorization are all manually triggered, permissioned single-cycle calls with no timer, keeper, or upkeep integration. The owner's 'every N minutes, adjustable in a dashboard' requirement is Phase 2 scope (per repo facts) and has zero on-chain scaffolding here (no Chainlink Automation / Gelato-style registration, no cron-like state).

No pro-rata-to-holders distribution logic in this file set: consumePayoutAuthorization moves the full rootSum to `hook` in one transfer; whatever computes/streams the pro-rata split to individual HKMN holders lives elsewhere (not in this unit) or does not yet exist.

No dashboard-facing read surface beyond raw Solidity view functions (readPendingAuthorization, readActiveAuthorization, isNonceConsumed, etc.) -- no events or views summarizing 'is a cycle currently stuck', elapsed time since FUNDED/OUTBOUND, or expected-vs-actual timing, which a monitoring dashboard would need to detect and surface a stuck cycle in the first place.

Route executor is INTEGRATION_PENDING (IPegCycleRouteExecutor is a bare 1-function interface with no implementation in this file set) -- the Collector Crypt pack-buy/open/sell leg that the owner's entire cycle depends on cannot execute at all yet from this unit's code alone.

suspicions.note: recordTerminalFailure only reachable from lifecycle==OUTBOUND and only when current USDG balance==0; combined with authorizePayout's exact-balance/minimum-return requirement, there is no valid lifecycle transition for a nonzero-but-below-minimumReturnUsdg return -- see autonomyGaps. This looks like a genuine missing state, not just a design choice, since the struct already carries minimumReturnUsdg as a real threshold that can legitimately be missed by a small margin.

Docstring says 'Immutable single-cycle USDG custody' but the state machine explicitly loops PAYOUT_COMMITTED back to accepting a new authorizeFunding, i.e. the contract is designed for repeated sequential cycles, not one cycle. Either the docstring is stale (likely, given codex/phase2-revision-57's 'per-cycle CREATE2 return escrow' suggests Phase 2 intends a genuinely fresh vault per cycle) or the multi-cycle reuse in Phase 1 is unintentional/undocumented behavior worth confirming with the spec author.

_transferExact demands result.length == 32 and decodes a strict bool from USDG.transfer. If the actual deployed USDG proxy implementation ever returns no data (some upgradeable/legacy ERC20 patterns do) this reverts every transfer unconditionally; this has not been verified against the live bytecode at 0x5fc5360D0400a0Fd4f2af552ADD042D716F1d168 in this review (out of scope for this unit's file list) and should be checked before mainnet integration.

Constructor validates the vault's authorizer against programmable/treasury/operations/this, and validates operations against vaultRouteExecutor/vaultUsdg, but never validates programmable or treasury against vaultRouteExecutor/vaultUsdg, nor validates vaultRouteExecutor/vaultUsdg against `address(this)`. Likely benign given routeExecutor/usdg are external fixed contracts, but the asymmetry in which pairs are checked looks like an incomplete enumeration rather than an intentional narrowing.

_bindCycleOperations is a one-line wrapper that just calls _bindCycleOperationsTrigger with identical arguments and identical access checks (msg.sender==_operations && trigger==_operations) -- currently dead/duplicate code in this file set (ProcessBudget.openPegCycle calls _bindCycleOperationsTrigger directly, not _bindCycleOperations); worth confirming whether another module (outside this unit) actually calls the wrapper, otherwise it's removable.

authorizePayout requires IPegCycleUsdg(usdg).balanceOf(address(this)) == authorization.rootSum at authorization time, then consumePayoutAuthorization re-checks the same equality at consumption time (line 283). Between those two calls (both authorizer- and hook-gated, presumably same block or very close), any USDG balance drift (e.g. a completely unrelated direct transfer into the vault by a third party, which nothing prevents since transfer() is permissionless) would revert consumePayoutAuthorization with TokenBalanceDeltaMismatch and require a fresh authorizePayout cycle -- low severity but worth noting the vault has no sweep/rescue function for accidental/dust inbound transfers at any lifecycle stage.

keyFacts: REQUIREMENTS_REVISION = 56 (PegCycleVault.sol:20) -- both FundingAuthorization and PayoutAuthorization must carry exactly this value; repo facts elsewhere reference 'requirements revision 57' for the unmerged Phase 2 line (codex/phase2-revision-57), confirming this Phase 1 vault is pinned one revision behind Phase 2's spec.

TOTAL_FEE_BPS=300 (3.00%), PROGRAMMABLE_FEE_BPS=10 (0.10%), TREASURY_FEE_BPS=40 (0.40%) in FeeAccounting.sol:9-11; process share is the implicit remainder = 250 bps (2.50%). Matches the repository-authoritative split named in the owner target.
solidity pragma pinned exactly to 0.8.26 in all 5 files (no floating pragma).
PegCycleVault.Lifecycle enum ordinal order: EMPTY(0), FUNDED(1), OUTBOUND(2), RETURNED(3), PAYOUT_COMMITTED(4), FAILED(5).

FundingAuthorization has 19 fields; PayoutAuthorization has 15 fields (IPegCycleVault.sol:5-44) -- both include requirementsRevision, chainId, cycleId, hook, vault, usdg, operationsTrigger, bindingManifestDigest, expiresAt, nonce as shared/repeated identity+replay fields.

FundingAuthorization-only fields: amount, outboundActionDigest, returnActionDigest, returnDestination, minimumRobinhoodReceive, minimumSolanaReceive, minimumReturnUsdg, robinhoodNativeGasCap, solanaNativeGasCap -- names strongly imply the outbound leg crosses from Robinhood Chain to Solana (Collector Crypt) and back, consistent with the owner's Collector-Crypt-pack narrative.

PayoutAuthorization-only fields: payoutId, manifestDigest, rootHash, rootSum, returnReceiptDigest -- rootHash/rootSum naming suggests a Merkle-root-based holder payout manifest (pro-rata distribution proof) that is verified/consumed elsewhere, not in this file set.
Test file sizes/counts: MoneyRoles.t.sol 610 lines/11 tests, ProcessBudget.t.sol 560 lines/12 tests, PegCycleVault.t.sol 883 lines/21 tests (44 total, no skip markers found).

openQuestions: Is the FAILED-is-permanently-terminal design (no recovery function) an intentional Phase 1 simplification that Phase 2's per-cycle CREATE2 vault (codex/phase2-revision-57) is meant to fix by simply discarding and redeploying a fresh vault per cycle, or is it an oversight that needs a Phase 1 patch given the owner's explicit 'restart/kick stuck cycles' dashboard requirement?

What is the intended contract-level (not just off-chain/dashboard) behavior for a partial/degraded return that is nonzero but below minimumReturnUsdg -- is a new lifecycle transition (e.g. a 'DEGRADED' or 'WRITE_OFF' state, or relaxing recordTerminalFailure's balance==0 check to balance<minimumReturnUsdg) planned?

Has the live USDG proxy at 0x5fc5360D0400a0Fd4f2af552ADD042D716F1d168 been confirmed to return a strict `true` (32-byte bool) from transfer(), given _transferExact's hard requirement on that exact return shape? (Out of scope for this unit's file list; flagged for the integration-readiness reviewers.)

Who/what actually calls MoneyRoles._bindCycleOperations (vs. the near-identical _bindCycleOperationsTrigger used directly by ProcessBudget.openPegCycle) -- is it consumed by code outside this file set, or is it dead code?

Is `authorizer` in PegCycleVault (and the constructor-time cross-checks in ProcessBudget) intended to be an EOA/multisig operated directly by 'operations' personnel, or is there meant to be an off-chain signature-verification layer that this Phase 1 code has not yet implemented (i.e. authorizeFunding/authorizePayout currently trust msg.sender==authorizer alone, with no signature over the struct)?

Does anything outside this file set ever call PegCycleVault's view getters (readPendingAuthorization, isCycleConsumed, etc.) to power the community-facing status dashboard the owner asked for, or would that need to be built from scratch against this ABI?
